Seminar Title:

High-entropy alloy (HEA) and Refractory high-entropy alloy (RHEA) coating by laser cladding method for improved mechanical properties

Seminar Hall, Mechaical Engineering Department (ME001)

Contact:

Manoj Masanta

Abstract:

High-entropy alloys (HEAs), composed of five or more elements in equal or near-equal molar ratios, have potential applications in aerospace engine components, cryogenic systems, biomedical components, and functional coatings owing to their unique properties. Refractory high-entropy alloys (RHEAs), consisting of two or more refractory metals, are promising materials for wear-resistant applications at elevated temperatures. Laser cladding of HEA coatings has emerged as an effective approach to enhancing the performance of components operating under severe environmental and tribological conditions. The present work focuses on the fabrication of Fe&ndashCo&ndashCr&ndashNi&ndashTi HEA and Ni&ndashCo&ndashCr&ndashMo&ndashW RHEA coatings on SS304 stainless steel and Ti6Al4V alloy substrates. The coating fabrication process has been optimized to achieve uniform layer thickness and improved hardness. The developed coatings have been characterized using scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and X-ray diffraction (XRD), while their mechanical performance has been evaluated through microhardness measurements. Future work will focus on optimizing various laser cladding parameters, including powder composition, layer thickness, number of layers, laser power, scanning speed, and focal position, to achieve high-quality clad layers.
